finding.claim: Broken authorization on DELETE /reports/:id: the async authorize() call is not awaited, so its 403 rejection is never observed and the report is deleted regardless of grants. Any authenticated user without a 'delete' grant can delete any report by id. Because the rejection is unhandled, on modern Node it may also crash the process.
finding.source: Authenticated low-privilege user sends DELETE /reports/<id> (req.params.id) for a report they have no 'delete' grant on

trace.note: DELETE handler entry; req.params.id is attacker-controlled
report loaded by id with no ownership scoping
authorize(...) called without await or return; the returned promise is discarded
the check runs asynchronously and throws 403 only inside the discarded promise
db.reports.remove executes immediately, without waiting on the grant check

finding.guards_checked: authorize() is correct in isolation (server.js:9-16), and the sibling PUT handler awaits it (server.js:27). The DELETE handler discards the result, so the control does not apply. There is no other middleware: the app-level middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user and does no access check.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 on a missing grant, but the DELETE handler calls it without await at server.js:20. The only middleware (server.js:4-7) copies the session user and checks nothing. The PUT handler awaits it correctly at server.js:27.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls the async authorize() as a bare statement, so its 403 throw at server.js:14 lands in a discarded promise and db.reports.remove at server.js:21 runs for any authenticated user, regardless of grants.
